cues.text: So what do these numbers mean? x equals one, y equals two, z equals three is the single point where all three planes meet.
Echelon form also reveals the structure. Here every column of A has a pivot, so there are no free variables, and the solution is unique.

But elimination can end differently. Ours ended with a pivot in every column. If instead a row becomes zero, zero, zero, bar five, it says zero equals five. That's impossible, so there is no solution: the planes share no common point.

And if a row becomes all zeros, including the right-hand side, that equation added no new information. A variable is then free, and there are infinitely many solutions, like planes meeting along a line.
So after elimination, the pivots tell you everything: one solution, none, or infinitely many.
